findings.location: Proof 1.1, line 95: sorting biconditional and description of J.
findings.evidence: Minimal-right representatives do not characterize sorting a fixed tuple: for a=(1,0), K is trivial, every permutation is minimal-right, and only the transposition sorts a. Also J permutes positions within columns, rather than permuting columns. Replace the biconditional by the unique minimum of the sorting right K-coset and correct the J action.

The tensor Hecke action and its bar-preserving signed/parameter transport are not established. At v=s, the trivial-induced cyclic swap gives the opposite correction sign from the actual source bar. Step 2.2 also assumes that the inverse tensor L matrix equals the spherical multiplicity matrix; the cited KL inversion theorem supplies generic matrix inversion, not that coefficient identification. Supply the explicit action, bar comparison, complementary-chart coefficient identity and signed wedge transport. Brundan, arXiv:math/0509700, Section 4, pp. 10–13, provides the relevant source argument.

The tensor/wedge coefficient bridge and its reverse-column version are asserted without constructing the Hecke action or proving the complementary-chart identification. Ordinary singular multiplicities, Weyl characters and abstract Fock pairings do not identify these independent matrices. Consequently the canonical coefficient 1 has not been proved to be an actual standard multiplicity in X(B), so the linkage edge remains unsupported. Prove the bridge independently; citing the later block-dependent KL theorem would introduce a cycle.

findings.evidence: The completed Hecke algebra and Frobenius partial centres do not establish the categorical structure of E^jS.
